metadata.title: Results from the Teacher Knowledge Survey: What Teachers Know About General Pedagogy

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The Teacher Knowledge Survey (TKS) is implemented as a module within TALIS 2024 and is administered to lower secondary (ISCED 2) teachers in the sampled schools. The report notes that when principal questionnaire variables are analysed at the teacher level, principal responses are treated as teacher-level attributes and the results are weighted by teacher weights; when principal data are linked to multiple teachers (e.g., school size), findings are interpreted as “share of teachers in schools”. The document does not provide the specific weight variable name(s) or replicate-weight scheme, so the exact weighting mechanics cannot be fully reconstructed from the excerpt. Because this is a descriptive/correlational OECD report (not an ML training paper), readers should rely on the TALIS 2024 Technical Report and TALIS 2024 User Guide for the precise complex-sample weighting and variance estimation procedures used in the underlying analyses.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This publication is a results report for the Teacher Knowledge Survey (TKS) within TALIS and does not describe an analysis pipeline that uses cognitive-domain Plausible Values (PV) in the PISA/TIMSS sense. Instead, it reports teacher general pedagogical knowledge (GPK) proficiency levels and many other outcomes based on self-reports from teachers and principals, and it explicitly states that the design does not support causal claims. Missing-data handling is not specified in the provided text excerpt; however, the report does describe non-reporting symbols (e.g., too few observations, item non-response thresholds) used in tables, which indicates that missingness is handled through reporting suppression/adjudication rather than a fully documented imputation strategy.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: TKS 2024 was administered to lower secondary education teachers (ISCED level 2) in the same schools sampled for the core TALIS 2024 survey. The report cautions that some countries/territories may not meet TALIS technical standards for participation rates, increasing non-response bias risk; however, the excerpt does not specify the exact inclusion/exclusion rules used to form the analytic sample. For table reporting, the report uses adjudication/reporting conventions where estimates may be suppressed when categories do not apply, when there are too few observations (e.g., fewer than 30 teachers or 10 schools/principals with valid data), or when item non-response rates exceed 50%, indicating that analytic outputs are restricted by applicability and minimum valid-observation thresholds.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD TALIS/TKS report summarizes results from the Teacher Knowledge Survey (TKS) 2024, a module within TALIS administered to lower secondary (ISCED 2) teachers in eight participating countries (Chile, Croatia, Morocco, Poland, Portugal, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, and the United States). The report describes TKS as including an assessment of teachers’ general pedagogical knowledge (GPK) alongside contextual questionnaires, with many other variables based on self-reports from teachers and principals. It explicitly states that the TKS design does not allow causal interpretations; reported relationships should be read as statistical associations. The report also provides guidance on international averages (OECD average-4 and TKS average-8) and on reporting suppression rules for non-reported estimates (e.g., too few observations or high item non-response). While it references relationships between teachers’ GPK and student outcomes on PISA, the excerpt does not provide the underlying model specifications or any machine-learning training/evaluation details.
